transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-24
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Lowe (Redwood SE), Mark Reynolds (Bluecrest - Head of ML), Priya Menon (Bluecrest - VP Eng), Carlos Díaz (Bluecrest - Cloud Architect)

Summary:
Brief check-in for upcoming renewal (June 2026) and discussion of expansion: increasing committed GPUs, adding a second region (EU), and contract extension terms; security and network details discussed; agreed to run a two-region benchmark and Redwood to send updated committed capacity pricing.

Topics:
- Renewal term and pricing
- Dedicated capacity vs hosted bursting
- Multi-region deployment (US + EU)
- Security: SOC2, audit logs, KMS
- Benchmark plan and timeline

Transcript:
[00:00] Samira: hey everyone thanks for joining, this is samira from Redwood, i'll kick us off - we wanted to do a quick renewal and expansion check in, make sure the capacity numbers still line up and go over the region asks.
[00:12] Mark: yeah thanks, samira. appreciate it. we've been using the dedicated pool for a few months, it's been solid. throughput is good, latency looks fine for most requests but we're seeing spikes during peak ETL windows.
[00:23] Ethan: got it. can you describe the spike characteristics? is it concurrency, long sequences, or particular endpoints?
[00:28] Mark: mostly concurrency - our batch inference jobs cause a bunch of long-running sessions, and the kv-cache hit rate drops during those. also some of the chat endpoints that have tool-calls are a little chatty.
[00:39] Ethan: okay makes sense - we have a couple levers: increase dedicated capacity (more GPUs), enable smarter autoscale/burst policies, and tune batching + prefix caching. i can share a config that favors low-latency interactive endpoints while still allowing batching for batches.
[00:53] Priya: quick q - from a cost perspective, what's the delta if we add another 8xA100 pool vs using hosted burst for peaks?
[01:01] Samira: good question. ballpark: adding a dedicated 8x pool reduces per-token cost at heavy sustained loads but has commit fees. hosted burst is more flexible but unit cost is higher. i will send a side-by-side with our math (expected utilization assumptions).
[01:13] Carlos: and region-wise, we need EU region for GDPR processing; currently most traffic is us-west. what's the work to spin up a second region with dedicated capacity?
[01:22] Ethan: technically we can provision dedicated capacity in eu-west-1, similar stack. there's networking considerations - VPC peering, private control plane options for Private deployments, and KMS cross-region key usage if you want encryption at rest with customer-managed keys. the team has done this for other customers.
[01:36] Mark: are there any performance differences in the runtime across regions? we saw an older note about kernel differences or quantization issues on different infra.
[01:43] Ethan: we test kernel selection and quant profiles per region/hardware. differences are usually small; if you pin model variants we can ensure consistent policy. there was a mis-doc earlier where a kernel mismatch impacted a microsecond-level perf, but we resolved that.
[01:55] Priya: on the contract terms - we're up for renewal in june. we want a 12 month extension with an option to add on another 50% capacity mid-term if needed. possible?
[02:05] Samira: yes that's a common pattern. we can draft a contract with a baseline commit and an add-on clause for capacity increases at predefined pricing breaks. would you want the add-on to be immediate, or require 30 days notice plus a pricing adjustment?
[02:17] Priya: prefer quick turnaround, like 7-14 days, but with defined pricing. we need predictability.
[02:22] Samira: reasonable. i'll propose a 14-day add-on window in the draft and include the pricing tiers.
[02:27] Mark: on compliance, can you confirm SOC2 and audit log retention? we may need 3 years of logs for the audit.
[02:33] Ethan: Redwood has SOC 2 Type II; we can also export audit logs at retention configurable per account. default retention is 365 days, but enterprise options extend that. i'll attach the compliance pack.
[02:43] Carlos: and SSO - we need SAML + SCIM and RBAC mapped to our groups.
[02:48] Samira: yes, SAML, SCIM are supported. we also have per-route RBAC in the console. we'll include the admin guide.
[02:55] Mark: about benchmarks - can we run a two-region latency test (us-west + eu-west) with a mixed workload: 60% interactive chat (short seq) and 40% batch long sequences. want to see tail latency and cost delta.
[03:07] Ethan: sounds good. for the benchmark we usually run a synthetic workload with your average prompt distribution, and measure p50/p95/p99 and token cost. i'll draft the plan - target 72 hour run to capture diurnal effects.
[03:18] Priya: timeline? we'd like results before we finalize the contract.
[03:21] Samira: we can schedule the benchmark week of 3/30 so you get results by the first week of April - leaves time for contract updates in May/June.
[03:30] Carlos: note - networking constraints: we have a transit gateway in us-west-2 and strict firewall rules for eu; i need to share the exact CIDR ranges and peering requirements.
[03:39] Samira: perfect, please send those - i'll loop in our infra team.
[03:43] Mark: pricing question: if we compare an 8x to 16x pool, how does autoscale behave? can we have a baseline small pool plus a burst pool?
[03:51] Ethan: yes you can have a primary dedicated pool and a burst pool; autoscale policies can spin up the burst pool or fall back to hosted API. we recommend a primary for predictable baseline latency and a burst for cost efficiency.
[04:02] (crosstalk) Priya: and what about quality regressions when we switch model variants in a fallback? we need eval hooks.
[04:08] Ethan: Redwood Optimize has quality monitoring and regression alerts tied to eval prompt sets. you can configure a canary deployment and automated rollback on regressions.
[04:17] Mark: ok good. earlier we saw an issue where a canary picked a quantized variant that changed tokenization slightly - not catastrophic but noticeable. is that still an issue?
[04:26] Ethan: we flagged that and added stricter pre-deploy evals for quantized variants. we'll include the release notes.
[04:32] Samira: quick note on commercial - if you commit to 12 months and the extra capacity, i can offer a modest discount on the add-on tiers; i'll include numbers in the quote.
[04:41] Priya: appreciate that. can we also get a CPU fallback option for extremely low-priority batch to save cost?
[04:47] Ethan: yes, you can route extremely low priority jobs to a CPU cluster, lower cost but much higher latency. good for nightly heavy batches.
[04:54] Carlos: regarding KMS - we prefer customer-managed KMS in us-west and eu-west; any gotchas?
[04:59] Ethan: cross-region CMK usage requires careful rotation policies; we can either replicate keys or have region-specific keys and handle decryption at region. our security docs cover best practices; will share.
[05:08] Mark: competitive note - we've also had conversations with Anthropic and Lambda Labs; one advantage for Redwood is the unified console and the rollout tooling, which we like.
[05:18] Samira: grateful to hear that. i'll make sure the quote maps to the features you highlighted.
[05:22] (brief silence)
[05:30] Samira: recap and next steps: 1) samira to send updated committed capacity pricing and contract draft by 2026-03-26; 2) ethan to prepare benchmarking plan and scripts - start week of 2026-03-30; 3) carlos to send VPC details and CIDR ranges by 2026-03-25; 4) samira to share SOC2 pack and audit log retention options.
[05:49] Priya: sounds good. one more question - what happens to data residency if we add the eu region mid-contract? do we need a contract amendment?
[05:57] Samira: usually we add a short amendment for region additions and note any pricing changes; we'll bake that into the add-on clause.
[06:04] Mark: great. any blockers on our side?
[06:06] Priya: none right now, just need internal sign off for the extra commit.
[06:10] Samira: ok we'll follow up with the docs and quote. thanks everyone.

(End of call)

Notes about transcript quality: automatic transcription with occasional mis-heard words (e.g., 'kv-cache' sometimes transcribed as 'kay v cash', product names sometimes missing capitalization). Action items captured above.
